questions.q: Why is "debit always means increase" a dangerous misconception?
options: Because debit always means decrease instead
Because only credit entries actually affect account balances
Because whether a debit increases or decreases an account depends entirely on the account's type
Because debits only apply to cash accounts
questions.explain: A debit increases debit-normal accounts (assets, expenses) but decreases credit-normal accounts (liabilities, equity, revenue).

questions.q: A journal entry has a $500 debit and a $450 credit. What should you conclude?
options: This entry is wrong — total debits must equal total credits exactly
This is close enough and can be posted as-is
This is normal as long as the amounts are both positive
The $50 difference will self-correct on the next transaction
questions.explain: Every transaction, with no exceptions, must have total debits exactly equal to total credits.

questions.q: What does it mean to pick the "wrong account, even with the right side"?
options: The debit and credit totals don't balance
The entry is balanced and arithmetically correct, but records the wrong story because the wrong account was chosen
The entry has no debit at all
This situation can never actually happen
questions.explain: An entry can be perfectly balanced in dollars while still misclassifying what actually happened — for example, recording loan principal entirely as interest expense.

questions.q: What is the correct way to think about an account's "normal balance"?
options: It is the only balance that account is legally allowed to have
It only applies to liability accounts
It changes randomly from month to month
It is the typical, expected side an account sits on — a deviation is worth investigating, not automatically wrong
questions.explain: A normal balance tells you what to expect. An abnormal balance (like an overdrawn Cash account) is a prompt to investigate, not necessarily an error.

questions.q: Which of these mistakes can Oracle Fusion's system-level validation reliably catch on its own?
options: A human correctly balancing an entry that tells the wrong financial story
Whether the accountant chose the conceptually correct account for a transaction
An unbalanced journal entry, since the system enforces debits equal to credits
All four mistakes, with no human judgment required
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion enforces balanced journals at the system level, but it cannot fully replace the human judgment needed to choose the right accounts for a transaction's story.
